instructions: Put 3 cups of water and the rice in a pot with a pinch of salt and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, until the water is gone. Leave it covered off the heat until the stew is ready.
Finely chop the onions. Mince the garlic and 1 tbsp of the ginger. Dice the tomatoes.
Melt the ghee in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onions with 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook, stirring often, for 6 minutes, until they're soft and starting to turn golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds. Then add 2 tsp of the berbere and the cardamom and stir for 1 minute, until it smells toasty and the onions are fairly dry.
Add the beef and the remaining 1 tsp of salt. Break it up with a wooden spoon and cook, stirring now and then, for 6 minutes, until there's no pink left and no big lumps.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup of water. Bring it to a simmer, then cook uncovered, stirring now and then, for 8 minutes, until the stew is thick and the oil has pooled at the edges.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Serve the stew over the rice or with injera, and put the last 1 tsp of berbere in a small bowl on the table for anyone who wants more heat.
method_notes: Two Sleevers (the lead) cooks onion, garlic and berbere in ghee until dry before the beef goes in, then adds tomato and a little water; Yewoin's mild family version uses clarified butter, cardamom and ginger and simmers longer in more water. I followed the lead's order on the stove (no pressure cooker), added the cardamom and ginger from the mild version, and used less berbere in the pot (2 tsp for 1 1/2 lb) with the rest on the table to keep the base mild. Food.com's page showed only one review and no star rating.
